newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Arab Investment Co to seek capital rise in June.
newsitem.headline: Arab Investment Co to seek capital rise in June.

text.p: The board of directors of the Arab Investment Company (TAIC) has deferred a proposal to raise its paid-in capital to a shareholders' meeting in June, the company said on Monday.

It said the board "reviewed a proposal to raise the capital to $400 million from $300 million" and decided to ask TAIC's shareholders about the move at an extraordinary meeting in June in the Saudi capital Riyadh.
It gave no further details, but said requests from Algeria and Lebanon to join TAIC would also be discussed in June.
TAIC current shareholders are Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Sudan, Egypt, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Syria, Iraq, Jordan, Tunisia, Morocco, Libya, Oman and Yemen.
It was established in 1974 by the 15 Arab states to invest money in Arab projects. It posted a $28 million profit in 1996, up from $18.4 million in 1995.
